title: dinostomp eval spec
description: One experiment: a question, data, models, a witnessed scorer, and a run budget. Written by humans or LLMs. Nothing runs until this validates.

question.description: The one question this eval answers. One sentence.

entitled_claims.description: Prose claims, human-interpreted. Prefer typed `claims`, which compile into evidence requirements the battery checks off.

claims.description: Typed claims: executable specifications of required evidence. C1 gates on these; the spec chooses its own bar by declaring one.

model.description: A model named in this spec, or 'each'.

min.description: The interval's LOWER bound must clear this; a point estimate above it does not entitle.

path.description: Path relative to the spec file. The linter rejects absolute paths and traversal.

render_choices.description: Append a lettered option block to every choice item's prompt, rendered by dinostomp rather than baked into your input text. Hands the tool ownership of option ORDER, which is what makes `--probe shuffle` (and P9, presentation-order sensitivity) possible at all.

separator.description: Splits `target` and `choices` cells into lists, e.g. "|". A flat CSV cell holds one string, so without this a multi-target item or an option list cannot be expressed in CSV at all. Cells that do not contain the separator stay plain strings, so declaring one never reshapes single-valued data.

fields.description: Optional mapping from this dataset's column names onto the canonical item fields.

mounts.description: Files OUTSIDE the pod that this eval depends on, e.g. a scorer shared across a workspace. Declaring a path is what makes it legal to reference: an undeclared path that leaves the pod is refused, because an unhashed input is outside the drift boundary. Every mount is hashed into each manifest as `mount_sha256`, so editing shared code after a run is drift exactly like editing the pod's own. Relative to the spec file; absolute paths are refused.

provenance.description: Who authored each part of the eval. Optional, but when present S16 reads it for self-referential construction: an eval whose questions, answer keys, scorer, and witnesses all trace to one author (especially one MODEL) has no independent check anywhere in it, and every guard that could catch a mistake was written by the mind that could have made it. Values are free strings; the convention is a 'human:' prefix for people (e.g. 'human:alice') and a bare model id otherwise (e.g. 'claude-opus-5'), because the model-graded-its-own-homework case is the one S16 warns hardest about.

keys_by.description: Who wrote or verified the answer keys (targets). Independence from items_by is what makes the keys trustworthy.

witnesses_by.description: Who wrote the scorer's witnesses. Independence from scorer_by is what stops the W1/W2/W3 gauntlet from being fitted to its own author's expectations.

review_by.description: An independent reviewer of the whole eval, if any. Its presence is the one thing that breaks a fully self-authored loop.

tools.description: Tools the harness offers a mediated agent: {name: 'file.py:symbol'}. Each is pod-local code, hashed into every manifest like a scorer, so swapping one between runs is drift. An agent on the mediated rail can reach a tool ONLY through the harness, which is what makes its trajectory a log rather than a claim. Required by provider `mediated` and meaningless without it.

isolation.description: How a mediated agent is run. Default `inprocess`: the agent shares this Python process, so the harness owns the TRACE but not the machine. `subprocess` runs it in a child with a credential-stripped environment, no tool code, a denied socket module and an enforced timeout. That is CONTAINMENT, not confinement: it defends a run against a careless or overreaching agent, not a machine against a hostile one. The filesystem is not confined and the network denial is defeatable; METHODOLOGY states exactly what each layer stops.

timeout_s.description: Wall-clock budget per item. The child is killed on expiry and the run stops cleanly with its ledger intact; a hang is contained rather than left to sit.

provider.description: dry is the offline deterministic provider: zero network, zero spend, always available. python mounts a pod-local callable (agent, RAG pipeline, workflow) on the target rail. imported declares a model this engine cannot call, whose evidence arrives via `dinostomp import`; `run` refuses it rather than inventing a way to produce the numbers itself. mediated mounts a pod-local agent whose TOOLS the harness holds, so the recorded trajectory is observed rather than self-reported; it takes answer(item, tools, ctx) and requires a top-level `tools` block. It is not a security sandbox and the docs say why.

entrypoint.description: Pod-local callable this target mounts. `python` takes run(item, ctx) and writes its own trajectory; `mediated` takes answer(item, tools, ctx) and cannot, because the harness holds the tools and records the calls itself. The file is hashed into every manifest, so editing it after a run is drift.

price_in.description: Input rate, USD per MTok, for a model the built-in table does not know. Declared HERE rather than passed on the command line so the rate is inside spec_sha256: the price a run was charged at becomes part of the drift boundary instead of a flag nobody recorded. Per model, because a fleet does not share one rate.

price_out.description: Output rate, USD per MTok. Must accompany price_in.

trajectory.description: Declarative policy over what a target may and must do while answering. Judge-free by construction: these are facts about the recorded trace, not opinions about it. Checked by T1-T6. The trust boundary depends on the rail: a `python` target SELF-REPORTS its trace, so these verify the RECORD and not the EXECUTION; a `mediated` agent's trace is written by the harness, and forbidden_tools and max_steps are additionally ENFORCED at call time rather than audited afterwards.

required_tools.description: Every trajectory must contain a call to each of these. T2 gates.

forbidden_tools.description: No trajectory may contain a call to any of these. T1 gates.

max_steps.description: A trajectory longer than this is a runaway. T3 gates.

output.description: A verbatim model output to feed the scorer.

target.description: The reference answer for this witness case.

expect.description: The verdict this case must produce. uncheckable pins the scorer's behavior on unparseable output, which is what kills the uncheckable-credit mutant.

expect_value.description: Optional graded credit in [0,1] this case must produce, for a scorer that emits partial credit. Pinning an INTERMEDIATE value (0<v<1) is what proves the scorer actually grades rather than returning 0/1 relabelled; W3 requires at least one such witness of any scorer that emits a graded value. Absent, only the verdict is checked.

params.description: Scorer options. numeric: `tolerance` (float) and `extract` (`first` or `last`) - `last` is what you want when models show their working, and R16 is the check that tells you they do. regex: `pattern`.

code.description: Path to a python file exposing score(output, target) -> bool. Required when kind=python.

rubric.description: What the judge is grading for, in one instruction. Hashed with the spec, so editing it after a run is drift.

cross_judge.description: A SECOND judge, from a different model family, read only by `--probe crossjudge`. Self-preference is not measurable with one judge: there is nothing to compare its leniency against. Two judges grading the same recorded outputs make it an interaction J4 can read.

judge.description: The model doing the grading. Required when kind=judge. Its calls are priced and capped like any other call.

allOf.description: At least one case the scorer must accept.
At least one case the scorer must reject. A scorer that cannot fail is not a scorer.

witnesses.description: Concrete cases the scorer must get right before it is allowed to score real data. Executed by the runner before every run.

seed.description: Required. There is no unseeded run.

seeds.description: Extra seeds to repeat the WHOLE eval under, each a separate run file. `seed` stays the primary. Measures the spread a single seed cannot: item selection and provider sampling both move, and P10 reports how far. A number that changes when only the seed changes was never the model's number.

budget_usd.description: Hard spend cap. Required even for free runs, so the field is never an afterthought.

judge_block.description: The model doing the grading. Required when kind=judge. Its calls are priced and capped like any other call: a judge is not free just because it is not the examinee.

provider.description: dry is the offline control judge (agrees with normalized exact match, no biases). python mounts a pod-local judge(output, target, ctx) -> str.

entrypoint.description: Required when the judge provider is python. Hashed into every manifest as judge_sha256.

price_in.description: Input rate, USD per MTok, for a judge model the built-in table does not know. A judge that cannot be priced cannot be capped, so without this a hosted judge outside the table refuses to run.

price_out.description: Output rate, USD per MTok. Must accompany price_in.

params.description: Sampling for the judge. temperature defaults to 0, because grading is not a creative task: a judge sampled hot contradicts itself on identical input, which J3 measures and the witness gate can fail at random.
